articles.title: ‘Demon-possessed individual’: Trump loyalist drops bonkers explanation for JD Vance feud
articles.description: Influential MAGA influencer Laura Loomer took to social media Saturday to dispel claims that she disliked Vice President JD Vance, explaining that her long-running feud with the vice president was only her trying to protect him from “a demon possessed individual.” “For the record, I do not dislike Vice President Vance. I just have a really good judge of character and the demon possessed trust fund kid who lives in Maine and pals around with jihadists and calls President [Donald] Trump the anti-Christ is a threat to our Vice President,” Loomer wrote on X to her nearly 2 million followers, referencing right-wing figure Tucker Carlson. “Tucker literally admitted he was attacked by a demon. I am trying to protect our Vice President from a demon possessed individual who wants to drag our country to hell.” Carlson did, in fact, claim to have been "physically mauled” by a demon in a 2024 interview, an attack, he claimed, that left him “bleeding and with still-visible scars,” according to Mediaite . Loomer has attacked Vance in the past on a range of issues, including for being “ friends with degenerates ,” and for compromising Republicans’ 2026 midterm prospects. Vance has also clapped back at Loomer, calling her attacks “disgraceful” earlier this year. And yet, Loomer insisted Saturday night that she held no grudge against Vance, and actually cared deeply about him. “I am trying to help our President and Vice President because I care about them,” Loomer wrote. “I wish people would understand.” A self-described “ proud Islamophobe ,” Loomer has a long history of making overtly racist and bigoted remarks, particularly against Muslims . Despite her frequent controversial remarks, she’s continued to wield “ breathtaking influence ” in the Trump White House, having played an outsized role in the administration’s mass firings and immigration policies . For the record, I do not dislike Vice President Vance. I just have a really good judge of character and the demon possessed trust fund kid who lives in Maine and pals around with jihadists and calls President Trump the anti-Christ is a threat to our Vice President. articles.title: A Dress With Pockets Is Functional And Flattering, And Zara's £39.99 Midi Is A Must-Have For Autumn
BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremony: Start Time, How To Watch, And What To Expect
articles.description: It's almost time for the first BlizzCon event in two years, as Blizzard prepares to celebrate its past, present, and future with its traditional opening ceremony. This leads into two days of panels and interviews, as Blizzard talks about its biggest franchises, ranging from Warcraft to Overwatch. If you're not planning to make a trip to Anaheim to watch the show in person, the good news is that you can enjoy it from the comfort of your home. Here's a breakdown of when you can tune in for all the announcements. How to watch the BlizzCon 2026 opening ceremony You can watch a livestream of the BlizzCon 2026 opening ceremony through Blizzard's official YouTube, Twitch, and Battle.net channels. YouTube Twitch Battle.net When to watch the BlizzCon 2026 opening ceremony The show kicks off at the following times on September 12, and it'll run for roughly 75 minutes. 10:30 AM PT 1:30 PM ET 5:30 PM GMT 6:30 PM BST 7:30 PM CET 2:30 AM JST (September 13) 3:30 AM AEST (September 13) Will the BlizzCon 2026 musical performance be livestreamed? Nope, the musical performance will be exclusive to BlizzCon 2026 attendees. This year's headline act features K-pop group Le Sserafim, and international music duo Yoasobi will perform during BlizzCon's first-ever esports halftime show in the Overwatch World Cup Arena. What to expect We've got a detailed breakdown of our expectations for BlizzCon 2026 , but to sum it up, we're expecting Warcraft, StarCraft, Diablo, and Overwatch to be in the spotlight. Blizzard is already teasing something for StarCraft, with most fans predicting that we could see a StarCraft shooter revealed or Nexon potentially developing the next entry in the franchise. This year marks the 30th anniversary of Diablo, so we wouldn't be too surprised to see the legacy games celebrated and maybe even a first look at a new Diablo 4 expansion. For Overwatch, we're expecting Blizzard to focus more than ever on the game's competitive side, so a reveal trailer for the next playable hero and a look at how the current Reign of Talon storyline will conclude look pretty likely. Over in Azeroth, the reveal of a new World of Warcraft expansion is also an easy bet. BlizzCon has been a launching ground for multiple WoW expansion reveals in the past, so we're getting our popcorn ready for when the company drops a cinematic trailer for The Last Titan. There might also be a new version of WoW Classic shown off, but overall, it looks like Blizzard fans are in for a bumper show to help kick off the BlizzCon weekend.
